metadata.title: TradeCheck
metadata.description: Multilingual pre-shipment check for commercial invoices, packing lists and purchase orders.

footer.notice: For information only — not official customs or legal advice.
footer.positioning: TradeCheck is a pre-shipment check you run yourself. It does not replace a customs broker or professional advice.

messages.arith-line-total: Line {line} of {document}: {quantity} × {unitPrice} = {expected}, but the line total is {actual}. Difference: {difference}.
messages.arith-sum-incomplete: {document}: {count, plural, one {# goods line has} other {# goods lines have}} no line total, so the lines could not be added up and compared with the document total.
messages.arith-sum-total: {document}: the line totals add up to {sum}, but the document total is {total}. Difference: {difference}. If freight, insurance, discounts or taxes explain it, check that they are shown on the document.
messages.arith-qty-sum: {document}: the line quantities add up to {sum}, but the printed total quantity is {total}.
messages.weight-net-gross: {document}: the net weight ({net}) is greater than the gross weight ({gross}).
messages.xdoc-packages: Number of packages differs: {valueA} in {docA}, {valueB} in {docB}.
messages.xdoc-incoterm-place: Incoterms® named place differs: “{valueA}” in {docA}, “{valueB}” in {docB}.
messages.xdoc-origin: Country of origin differs: {valueA} in {docA}, {valueB} in {docB}.
messages.xdoc-destination: Country of destination differs: {valueA} in {docA}, {valueB} in {docB}.
messages.xdoc-order-ref: {docA} refers to order {valueA}, but the purchase order number is {valueB} ({docB}).
messages.xdoc-order-ref-missing: {document} shows no order reference, so it could not be matched with the purchase order.
messages.xdoc-exporter-same: The exporter is written differently but names the same party: “{valueA}” in {docA}, “{valueB}” in {docB}.
messages.xdoc-exporter-unknown: The exporter is written differently: “{valueA}” in {docA}, “{valueB}” in {docB}. Whether both name the same party could not be verified.
messages.xdoc-importer-same: The importer is written differently but names the same party: “{valueA}” in {docA}, “{valueB}” in {docB}.
messages.xdoc-importer-unknown: The importer is written differently: “{valueA}” in {docA}, “{valueB}” in {docB}. Whether both name the same party could not be verified.
messages.xdoc-line-count: Number of goods lines differs: {countA} in {docA}, {countB} in {docB}. The descriptions were not compared line by line.
messages.xdoc-goods-different: Line {line}: the goods descriptions differ: “{valueA}” in {docA}, “{valueB}” in {docB}.
messages.xdoc-goods-unknown: Line {line}: the goods descriptions are written differently: “{valueA}” in {docA}, “{valueB}” in {docB}. Whether they describe the same goods could not be verified.
messages.xdoc-hs: Line {line}: the HS codes differ in the first six digits: {valueA} in {docA}, {valueB} in {docB}.
messages.fmt-value: {document}: “{value}” in {field} could not be read as a valid value. Correct it so that it can be checked.
messages.fmt-currency: {document}: {value} is not in the ISO 4217 currency list dated {listDate}. If it is a newer code, check it against the current list.
messages.fmt-country: {document}: {value} in {field} is not an ISO 3166-1 country code.
messages.fmt-country-user-assigned: {document}: {value} in {field} is a user-assigned code, not an official ISO 3166-1 country code.
messages.fmt-incoterm: {document}: {value} is not one of the 11 Incoterms® 2020 rules.
messages.fmt-incoterm-retired: {document}: {value} is from Incoterms® {edition} and is not part of Incoterms® 2020.
messages.fmt-incoterm-no-place: {document}: the Incoterms® rule {value} is given without a named place.
messages.fmt-hs-short: {document}, line {line}: the HS code {value} has fewer than six digits. The internationally harmonized part of an HS code is six digits.
messages.fmt-hs-expert: HS codes are checked for format only. TradeCheck does not verify the classification; have it confirmed by a customs expert.
messages.fmt-iban: {document}: the IBAN {value} is not valid (structure or check digits).
messages.date-order: {docB} is dated {dateB}, before the purchase order ({docA}, {dateA}).
messages.rec-field: {document}: {field} was not found. It is commonly shown on this type of document.
messages.req-weight-unit: {document}: {field} has no unit, so it cannot be compared with other documents.
messages.req-line-field: {document}: {field} is missing on {count} of {total, plural, one {# goods line} other {# goods lines}}.
messages.doc-not-read: {document} has not been read, so it is not included in the checks.
messages.docset-missing: Missing document: {documentType}. Comparisons with it were skipped.
messages.docset-optional: No purchase order in this check. The order reference and order date checks were skipped.
messages.docset-duplicate: More than one document of the type “{documentType}”. Only {document} was compared with the other documents.
messages.docset-other-type: {document} was not recognized as a commercial invoice, packing list or purchase order and was not compared. Change its type if it was recognized wrongly.
messages.docset-insurance: Under the Incoterms® rule {value} the seller obtains cargo insurance, so an insurance document is usually part of the shipment documents.
messages.docset-typical: Depending on the goods and the destination country, other documents may be required, such as a transport document, a certificate of origin, licences or certificates. Check the destination country's rules.
messages.docset-typical-country: Depending on the goods, other documents may be required for {country}, such as a transport document, a certificate of origin, licences or certificates. Check the rules of {country}.
messages.fmt-vat-id-greece: {document}: {field} {value} starts with GR. Greek VAT numbers use the prefix EL (EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC, article 215).
messages.fmt-vat-id-nl: {document}: {field} {value} does not have the structure of a Dutch VAT number: NL, 9 digits, the letter B and 2 digits, as published by the Belastingdienst.
messages.fmt-eori: {document}: {field} {value} does not have the structure of an EORI number: a two-letter country code followed by up to 15 letters or digits, as described by the European Commission.
messages.fmt-eori-nl: {document}: {field} {value} does not have the structure of a Dutch EORI number: NL followed by the 9-digit RSIN, according to the European Commission.
messages.xdoc-vat-id-seller: Seller's VAT number differs: {valueA} in {docA}, {valueB} in {docB}.
messages.xdoc-vat-id-buyer: Buyer's VAT number differs: {valueA} in {docA}, {valueB} in {docB}.
messages.xdoc-eori-seller: Seller's EORI number differs: {valueA} in {docA}, {valueB} in {docB}.
messages.xdoc-eori-buyer: Buyer's EORI number differs: {valueA} in {docA}, {valueB} in {docB}.

problem.title: One shipment, three documents, many places to disagree
problem.body: Sales writes the invoice, the warehouse writes the packing list and the buyer writes the purchase order. When a count, a weight, a party or an Incoterms® rule differs between them, the shipment can be held, a payment refused or a correction requested after the goods have left.

items.counts: Package counts and weights that differ between the invoice and the packing list
items.totals: Line totals that do not add up to the document total
items.terms: A currency, Incoterms® rule or country that changes from one document to the next
items.parties: The exporter or importer written differently on each document
items.missing: Missing order references, HS codes or dates

problem.statText: of documents presented under letters of credit are refused on first presentation, according to an estimate by the ICC Banking Commission.
problem.ruleText: Under UCP 600, article 14 (d), data in one document must not conflict with data in the other documents presented.
problem.ruleSource: ICC Uniform Customs and Practice for Documentary Credits
problem.scope: TradeCheck does not examine letters of credit. It checks that your own documents agree with each other before anyone else looks at them.

how.title: How a check works
how.lead: Four steps, in the order you do them.

add.title: Add the documents
add.body: PDF, PNG or JPG: up to {files} files per check, {mb} MB per file and {pages} pages per PDF. The document type is detected and can be changed.

read.title: Read them
read.body: An AI model transcribes each field together with the page and the text it came from. Low-confidence values are marked, and you can correct any value.

check.title: Run the checks
check.body: {count} deterministic rules compare totals, weights, parties, codes and dates across the documents. The same documents always give the same result.

share.title: Review and share
share.body: Every finding shows its evidence in the document. Print the report as a PDF or draft a correction e-mail to the person who issued the document.

checks.title: What every check covers
checks.lead: These are the rules that run today, grouped as in the report. A rule that does not apply is listed as not applicable, and anything that cannot be confirmed is marked “Could not be verified” — never guessed.

evidence.title: Every finding points to the page and the line
evidence.body: Each finding carries a reference tag such as F1. The same tag sits in the document margin beside the evidence, so you can go from a finding to the paperwork and back.

items.quotes: Verbatim quotes with the document name and page
items.corrected: Values you changed are labelled as corrected by you
items.zoom: On a phone the page zooms, and the marks stay on their text

hs.title: Classify your goods
hs.body: HS codes are checked for format and compared between your documents. TradeCheck never suggests a classification.

sources.title: Invent country rules
sources.body: Country-specific requirements can only be added as rule packs that cite their source. None ship today.

guess.title: Guess
guess.body: When a value is missing or a source cannot be reached, the result says “Could not be verified”.

advice.title: Replace professional advice
advice.body: Results are for information only. They do not replace a customs broker, a bank's document examination or legal advice.

ai.title: Use the model you trust
ai.body: Reading, name comparison, explanations and e-mail drafts each go to a model the operator configures: Anthropic, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint such as an LLM gateway, vLLM or Ollama.

items.schema: Every answer is checked against a schema before it is used
items.data: Document text is treated as data, never as instructions
items.tokens: The tokens used are shown on every check

items.local: Stored on the server you run, in a local database and folder
items.retention: {hours, plural, one {Deleted automatically after # hour; delete a check at any time} other {Deleted automatically after # hours; delete a check at any time}}
items.send: Sent to the AI provider only when you choose to read them
items.keys: API keys stay on the server, and the pages carry no tracking scripts

compliance.q: Does TradeCheck tell me whether my shipment is compliant?
compliance.a: No. It shows where your documents disagree with each other or contain invalid values, and lists every check that ran. It does not decide customs compliance and is not official advice.

documents.a: Commercial invoices, packing lists and purchase orders, as PDF, PNG or JPG. The documents can be in any language the configured model can read.

scans.a: Scans and photos are read as images by models that support them. Exact highlighting needs a text layer, so for scans the evidence is shown for the whole page.

retention.q: How long are my files kept?
retention.a: {hours, plural, one {Files, extracted data and findings are deleted automatically after # hour. You can delete a check yourself at any time.} other {Files, extracted data and findings are deleted automatically after # hours. You can delete a check yourself at any time.}}

corrections.q: Can I correct a value that was read wrongly?
corrections.a: Yes. Every extracted value can be edited. The checks run again straight away, and the value is labelled as corrected by you.

models.q: Which AI models does it use?
models.a: The ones the operator configures: Anthropic models or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Each task can use a different model.

lc.q: Does it check letters of credit or HS classification?
lc.a: No. It does not examine letters of credit and does not classify goods. HS codes are only checked for format and for consistency across your documents.

counterparty.q: Does TradeCheck verify that the seller or buyer is a real company?
counterparty.a: No. It checks VAT and EORI numbers for format and for consistency across your documents, and links to the European Commission's VIES and EORI services to confirm that a number is registered. Company registry, sanctions and credit checks are separate services.
